::: {#sol-deep-grad-norms}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Size of the weight gradient at each of the 11 layers of two deep networks, on a log scale.
#|   For the logistic network it falls by many orders of magnitude from the last layer to the first;
#|   for the ReLU network it falls by far less.
def deep_mlp(activation, n_hidden=10, width=32):
    _ = torch.manual_seed(0)
    layers, n_in = [], 64
    for layer in range(n_hidden):
        layers += [nn.Linear(n_in, width), activation()]
        n_in = width
    layers.append(nn.Linear(width, 10))
    return nn.Sequential(*layers)


grad_norms = {}
for name, activation in [("logistic", nn.Sigmoid), ("ReLU", nn.ReLU)]:
    net = deep_mlp(activation)
    loss_fn(net(x_train), y_train).backward()
    grad_norms[name] = [m.weight.grad.norm().item() for m in net if isinstance(m, nn.Linear)]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
for name, norms in grad_norms.items():
    ax.semilogy(range(1, len(norms) + 1), norms, marker="o", label=name);
ax.set_xlabel("layer (1 = first)");
ax.set_ylabel("size of weight gradient");
ax.legend();
plt.show()
shrink = {name: norms[-1] / norms[0] for name, norms in grad_norms.items()}
print(shrink)
```

The size of a matrix here is the square root of the sum of its squared entries.
In both networks the weight [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) is largest at the last layer.
With the [logistic function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-logistic-function),
the weight gradient shrinks at every layer going back,
and the last layer's weight gradient is about $10^{`r round(log10(py$shrink[["logistic"]]))`}$ times the first layer's.
With the [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu),
the weight gradient shrinks over the last few layers and then levels off,
and the last layer's is `r sprintf("%.0f", py$shrink[["ReLU"]])` times the first layer's.
A [training step](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-training-step) with one learning rate would move the logistic network's first layers almost not at all.

:::
